newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dollar up sharply, Euro shares advance.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dollar up sharply, Euro shares advance.

text.p: The dollar climbed to its highest levels against the yen for more than four years on Monday, while European stock markets were also in positive mood, celebrating a recovery on Wall Street.

The U.S currency, which also gained against the mark, was boosted by prospects for further increases in U.S. interest rates and comments by Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin that a firm dollar helped the U.S. economy.
"The dollar is well supported. Perceptions of higher U.S. rates are definitely helping." said a trader at a British bank.
The currency market took little notice of news that Japan's current account balance of payments surplus, a key source of trade friction with Washington, had widened again in February.
"The market largely shrugged off the current account data and everyone is buying dollars," said a dealer at a European bank in Tokyo.

Among key European stock markets welcoming a three-quarter percentage point rebound on Wall Street on Friday, Frankfurt was up more than two percent, Paris around 1.9 percent and London 0.6 percent by midmorning.

Paris share brokers said an informal weekend meeting of European finance ministers on economic and monetary union (EMU) had helped by easing market worries about delays in the timetable for the common euro currency.

But some uncertainty seemed to remain on Monday -- enough to make German Finance Minster Theo Waigel respond to press reports that he had softened his stance on the budget deficit criterion for EMU. He insisted that he opposed any looser interpretation of the rule.

The dollar was at its strongest levels for two weeks against the mark above 1.69 marks in early European business -- helped by progress at the weekend meeting towards a common currency, which would replace the mark.
But it was unable to hold all its gains against the yen and traded a little below a 50-month peak of 125 yen scored in late Asian trading.
"It's partly EMU, it's partly another speech from Rubin and a triggering of stops above 124.50 in dollar/yen," said Nick Parsons, foreign exchange strategist at Banque Paribas.
However, he cautioned: "There has not been a lot of follow-through and I think the risk is for a pull-back."
Tokyo traders tipped the U.S. currency to continue its advance against the yen, with few expecting the Bank of Japan to intervene openly to stem its rise.

Analysts said dollar bulls had been encouraged by the lack of acrimony during Rubin's visit to Japan last week when he again criticised Japan's ballooning trade surplus. On Monday, in Hanoi, he commented: "I think that the strength of the dollar that we've had for quite some time now has spurred low interest rates, low rates of inflation...in the United States.
"Having said that, I am not expressing any view...with regard to the level or direction that we would seek one way or another," Rubin added.
The dollar has risen steadily since hitting a post-war low just under 80 yen two years ago.
German shares kicked off the week on a stronger than expected note, seeking to catch up with Wall Street's firm close.
"What we are seeing is the typical short squeeze," said one trader, warning that investors could soon take some profits.
In London, Europe's biggest stock market marked share prices up on the back of the gains in New York and higher bond prices.

The Dow Jones industrial average of U.S. blue-chip stocks ended 48.72 points higher at 6,526.07 on Friday. But for the week as a whole it dropped 214.52 points -- the fourth biggest fall on record -- as investors fretted about rising U.S. interest rates.

Dealers said British shares would remain vulnerable to renewed weakness across the Atlantic as U.S. first-quarter corporate results emerged. Weekend press comments debating the chances of a significant U.S market correction would contribute to jitters among investors, they added.
"The key is still Wall Street," said one.

"I'm not sure anything has changed," said a senior London share dealer. "We're still worried about interest rates and inflation and we've got an election in front of us. But there's still a lot of cash around and the UK is the healthiest market in Europe."
French shares opened sharply higher, boosted by the revival on Wall Street and the progress made by the dollar, good news for exporting firms.
"We've had quite a bit of consolidation after the rise in U.S. interest rates and now we are going to rise in line with the dollar's recovery," one Paris share broker said.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei earlier fell 144.92 points or 0.81 percent to 17,715.67.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.6965 marks and 124.91 yen, up from 1.6768 and 124.23 in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0930 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 27.0 points or 0.64 percent at 4,263.6.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 77.10 points or 2.38 percent at 3,322.03.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was 47.70 points or 1.89 percent ahead at 2,565.67.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the morning at $347.85 an ounce, up a little from Friday's London close of $347.45. Silver added three cents to $4.76.
